questions.stem: A farmer uses large quantities of nitrogen-based fertiliser on their fields. After heavy rain, a nearby lake experiences an algal bloom, and fish begin to die. What process explains this sequence of events?

options.text: The fertiliser is directly toxic to the fish
Eutrophication: fertiliser runs off into the lake, causing excessive algal growth that blocks light, then decomposing algae use up dissolved oxygen, suffocating fish
The rain dilutes the lake water, making it too pure for fish
The fertiliser makes the water too warm for fish

questions.explanation: This is eutrophication: (1) fertiliser runs off into the water, adding excess nitrates and phosphates; (2) this causes rapid algal growth (algal bloom); (3) the algae block sunlight, killing underwater plants; (4) when the algae die, decomposing bacteria use up dissolved oxygen; (5) fish and other aquatic organisms suffocate due to lack of oxygen. It is the oxygen depletion, not the fertiliser itself, that kills the fish.

questions.stem: Drinking water must be treated before it is safe to consume. What is the purpose of adding chlorine to the water supply?

options.text: To make the water taste better
To kill harmful bacteria and other microorganisms that could cause disease
To remove dissolved minerals
To make the water acidic

questions.explanation: Chlorine is added to water as a disinfectant to kill bacteria, viruses, and other pathogens that could cause diseases such as cholera and typhoid. Only small amounts are needed, and the concentration is carefully controlled to be safe for drinking while still effective against microorganisms. This simple water treatment has saved millions of lives worldwide.

questions.stem: Heavy metals such as lead and mercury can enter water supplies from industrial waste. Why are heavy metals particularly dangerous pollutants?

options.text: They make the water change colour
They are toxic even in very small concentrations and accumulate in the body over time (bioaccumulation), causing organ damage
They make water more alkaline
They evaporate quickly and pollute the air instead

questions.explanation: Heavy metals are toxic at very low concentrations and cannot be broken down by the body. They accumulate in tissues over time (bioaccumulation) and can also increase in concentration up the food chain (biomagnification). Lead damages the nervous system, while mercury causes neurological damage. Once in water systems, heavy metals are very difficult to remove.

questions.stem: A water treatment plant uses several steps to purify water. Which is the correct order of treatment?

options.text: Chlorination → sedimentation → filtration
Filtration → chlorination → sedimentation
Sedimentation → filtration → chlorination
Chlorination → filtration → sedimentation

questions.explanation: Water treatment follows a logical sequence: (1) sedimentation — large particles settle to the bottom in settling tanks; (2) filtration — water passes through sand and gravel filters to remove smaller particles; (3) chlorination — chlorine is added to kill remaining microorganisms. Each step removes progressively smaller contaminants, with disinfection as the final step before distribution.

questions.stem: Sewage discharged into a river increases the biological oxygen demand (BOD). What does a high BOD indicate, and why is it harmful?

options.text: There is too much oxygen in the water
Microorganisms decomposing the sewage consume large amounts of dissolved oxygen, leaving too little for fish and other aquatic life
The water is too clean for organisms to survive
The water temperature is too high

questions.explanation: Biological oxygen demand (BOD) measures how much oxygen microorganisms need to decompose organic matter in water. Sewage is rich in organic matter, so decomposing bacteria multiply rapidly and consume dissolved oxygen. A high BOD means oxygen is being used up faster than it can be replaced, creating oxygen-depleted zones where fish and invertebrates cannot survive.
